items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Beta 4 (24 Sep) reverted four of the release's marquee features, and the project said why.
PG 19 GA slipped from September to "October", and the RC it was supposed to precede has not shipped.
MySQL 8.0 has been end-of-life since 30 April 2026, and Percona is now the only ongoing fix stream for that branch.
Nothing shipped from Oracle MySQL in the window; the next drop is the 20 Oct CPU. Newest upstream is 9.7.3 (18 Aug 2026).
MariaDB moved only its rolling line: 13.0.2 GA and 13.1.1 RC, both 15 Sep.
CockroachDB shipped v26.2.7 (21 Sep) and v25.4.17 (15 Sep); SQLite shipped nothing.
Vitess: six High advisories, no released fix, and nothing tracking one.
None of those Vitess advisories has a CVE id or an OSV record, while their lower-severity siblings do.
PgBouncer 1.26.0 (23 Sep) fixes two pre-authentication remote DoS bugs — patch this one.

Pgpool-II shipped seven CVEs across five branches (29 Sep): 4.7.3, 4.6.8, 4.5.13, 4.4.18, 4.3.21. Four are unauthenticated (PR:N): CVE-2026-92870 stack overflow from arbitrary-length failover message…
Those Pgpool CVSS v3 and v4 scores disagree in both directions, so your severity gate decides your answer.
No OLTP engine, pooler or managed-database entry appeared in CISA KEV this window.
btree_gist's inet/cidr GiST opclasses are fundamentally broken and will never be fixed — and this bites every supported PostgreSQL version today, not just 19. Tom Lane's commit is blunt…
PgBouncer was leaking SET search_path across clients in transaction pooling mode, and the fix only works on PostgreSQL 18+. 1.26.0 now tracks every parameter PostgreSQL reports by default…
REPACK and REPACK CONCURRENTLY land in core, retiring the pg_repack extension for most people.
Autovacuum gets parallel index workers and a scoring system that picks what to vacuum.
pg_plan_advice and pg_stash_advice put planner stabilisation in the tree.
A WAIT command gives you read-your-writes on standbys without routing back to the primary.
Logical replication finally replicates sequence values, and can be turned on without a restart.
pgvector 0.8.7 (1 Oct) fixes CVE-2026-103484 — and it is an IVFFlat-build bug only, which matters because the CVE text does not say so loudly.

Aurora PostgreSQL caught up to community on 29 Sep: 18.6, 17.11 and 16.15 all shipped that day.
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL removed cloudsql.instances.export from three predefined roles (28 Sep) — a breaking IAM change.
Spanner shipped automatic parameterization (18 Sep) and transactional queues GA (17 Sep).
Neon's backend went GA (18 Sep) and took the SDK to v6 as a breaking change.
Audit for the broken inet/cidr GiST indexes before you do anything else in this brief.
Test REPACK CONCURRENTLY against your current pg_repack runbook on a PG 19 beta.
Benchmark PG 19 with JIT off and max_locks_per_transaction deliberately set.
PostgreSQL 14 reaches end of life on 2026-11-12 — 35 days out. 14.24 is the final release, and it lands on the same day as the Nov minor release for every other branch, so there is no grace period…
Next PostgreSQL minor releases: 2026-11-12, then 2027-02-11, 2027-05-13, 2027-08-12.
Oracle's next Critical Patch Update is 2026-10-20 (12 days out), which is when MySQL 9.7.x and 8.4.x move.
MySQL 8.0 EOL was 2026-04-30 and has already passed — no upstream fixes for over five months.
MariaDB 10.6 EOL was 2026-07-06 and has already passed.
PG 19 breaking change — max_locks_per_transaction default goes 64 → 128, and tuned values must be doubled.
PG 19 breaking change — JIT is disabled by default, because "this costing has been determined to be unreliable." Analytical workloads on PostgreSQL must now enable it manually.

PG 19 breaking changes that block pg_upgrade outright: carriage returns or line feeds in database, role or tablespace names; and any btree_gist inet/cidr index.

PgBouncer 1.26.0 removes online restart (-R), SHOW FDS and SUSPEND. If your zero-downtime reload depends on takeover, it breaks on upgrade; the replacement is rolling restarts with so_reuseport.…
Vitess 23.0.8 / 24.0.5 do not exist and nothing is tracking them, so the six High advisories above have no fix date.
Two poolers in one month shipped unauthenticated-remote CVEs, and both were in the authentication handshake itself.
Fixes are now routinely arriving before, or without, the advisory and the identifier.

MongoDB 9.0 GA 2026-09-28, with 9.0.1 (security, CVE-2026-89099) and 9.0.2 released the same day.
The 8.2 branch is stranded, and this is the one item in this lane that demands action. 8.2 shipped September 2025, reached EOL 2026-07-31, and its last patch is 8.2.12 (2026-07-22) — three weeks…
The only unambiguous escape from 8.2 is a sequential binary upgrade to 8.3.9+ — and the two docs that describe the alternative contradict each other.
9.0 accepts upgrades only from 8.3 or 8.0 — 8.2 is not a documented source version.

mongosh 2.11.1 (09-15), 2.12.0 (09-18) and 2.13.0 (10-05) are housekeeping, but telemetry is the thread. 2.12.0 "re-enabled telemetry" (MONGOSH-3406) and 2.13.0 fixed telemetry being disabled by a…
8.3 made the Cost-Based Ranker the default plan-selection mechanism for eligible queries (multi-planning with CBR as backup).
9.0 adds a per-operation memory cap of 1 GB or 20% of server memory, whichever is greater.
$queryStats is restructured and now on by default, sampling 1% of reads and writes.
Server-side JavaScript is un-deprecated in 9.0 and now runs on a WebAssembly engine — with two sharp edges. $accumulator, $function, $where and mapReduce fail outright on ppc64le with no option to…
A multikey transition can now kill a running query.

8.2/8.3 changed two orphan-cleanup behaviors that affect secondary-read correctness.
Initial-sync index builds now take 10% of available RAM by default (floor 200 MB, ceiling 16 GB), and 9.0 raises diagnosticDataCollectionDirectorySizeMB from 200 to 500 MiB. Both are quiet…

mongosync cannot move you to 9.0, 8.3, 8.2 or 8.1 — this is the structural gap under the whole 8.2 problem.
removeShard is deprecated in 8.3, replaced by four explicit draining commands: startShardDraining, stopShardDraining, shardDrainingStatus, commitShardRemoval.
9.0 change streams return a new resumable error on election: InterruptedDueToReplStateChange (11602) when a stream's readPreference is no longer satisfied.

SERVER-136226 is an open 9.0 bug you must act on before upgrading a sharded cluster.

Atlas Infinite entered Public Preview in September: compute and storage are separate layers, and the unsupported list is the real spec.

Query Shape Insights now covers writes (update, insert, delete), not just find and aggregate.

Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore) is now "Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)" — and its service release notes have had no entry since the 2025-11-18 rename.
FerretDB has shipped nothing since v2.7.0 on 2025-11-10 — eleven months of silence, confirmed two ways.

Advisory-page staleness is now the dominant source error in this lane, and it fails in the reader's dangerous direction twice over.
The Mongo-compatible field has split into one vendor sprinting and two standing still.

Iceberg is adding a spec sentence because real engines check for exact type matches instead of honouring type promotion.
